company: Pursuit Attractions & Hospitality, Inc. (formerly Viad Corp)
drawdown_context: PRSU is the post-divestiture remnant of Viad Corp: on Dec 31, 2024 Viad sold its larger GES Exhibitions/Spiro business to Truelink Capital for $535M (gain on sale of $421.9M), repaid $393M of 2021 Credit Facility debt, mandatorily converted Crestview's Convertible Preferred Stock, and relaunched as a pure-play attractions company under PRSU ticker on Jan 2, 2025. The standalone continuing-ops business posted FY24 revenue of $366.5M and a continuing-ops net loss of $(51.8)M (loss of $(2.31) per share) driven by $47.6M of impairment charges and Jasper wildfire disruption. Going into the cutoff, the entity is a small-cap travel name (~28M shares, market cap mid-hundreds of millions) with a clean balance sheet ($14.7M of remaining debt outside finance leases), $200M of fresh undrawn revolver capacity, modest leverage, but a real-world identity rebranding wrapped around a CFO + CAO + CEO governance refresh and a goodwill base where Flyover already took a $14M impairment in 2024 (with $27.5M of asset impairment at Flyover Las Vegas) and Glacier Park Collection sits at an 11% cushion.

rfm_tuples.R: 'After a strategic review of the Company's operations, with the goal of increasing shareholder value, Pursuit (formerly known as Viad Corp) entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement... with TL Voltron, LLC... on October 20, 2024... The aggregate purchase price was $535 million, consisting of a base purchase price of $510 million... and a deferred purchase price of $25 million payable... one year after the closing date. On December 31, 2024, we completed the sale of the GES Business to Truelink Capital and relaunched as Pursuit Attractions and Hospitality, Inc... We began trading under a new NYSE ticker symbol, PRSU, on January 2, 2025.' Gain on sale recognized: $421.9M. $25M deferred proceeds recorded in Other current assets.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: divestiture / proceeds verification. Confirm transaction is bona-fide cash sale, structure of deferred-payment portion, use of proceeds, and that gain is GAAP-consistent. MODE B: identity-laundering check. Viad Corp's continuing operations carry a five-year stock chart that underperformed the SmallCap 600 H/R/L index ($63.19 vs $124.64 base-100 at YE2024). The act of renaming + new ticker + index-substitution in the performance graph is the textbook Mode B 'fresh-start framing' tell when bundled with a divestiture of the historically larger segment.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Transaction is GAAP-consistent (ASC 205-20 discontinued ops, $428.8M cash received in 2024 of the $535M total, $25M deferred receivable shown explicitly). Repayment of $393M 2021 Credit Facility within 24 hours of close is honestly disclosed. HOWEVER: the 5-year performance graph in Item 5 shows Pursuit/Viad at $63.19 (down 36.8% over 5 yrs) while S&P 500 reached $196.85 — a 260bps annualized deficit. The 10-K simultaneously CHANGES the comparator index set, dropping Media and Commercial Services & Supplies indices (which Viad had outperformed against in 2024) and keeping only SmallCap 600 H/R/L. This is the textbook 'change of comparator post-transformation' move that loses the historical underperformance baseline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The GES sale itself is well-disclosed and economically real ($421.9M gain, debt paid down, balance sheet cleaned). But the simultaneous (a) name change Viad to Pursuit, (b) new ticker PRSU, (c) ditching of the Media + Commercial Services comparators that previously surrounded Viad's stock-performance graph constitutes selective resetting of the investor reference frame. The historical 36.8% 5-year shareholder loss does not disappear because the ticker changed — but the new performance-graph framing makes it easier to forget. Mode B catch on identity rebranding.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On December 16, 2024, our Board of Directors appointed Michael Bo Heitz to serve as our Chief Financial Officer, effective upon the filing of this 2024 Form 10-K (the Effective Date). Mr. Heitz will succeed Ellen Ingersoll, Chief Financial Officer, who will step down from her role, on the Effective Date, and will continue to serve in an advisory role through March 31, 2025... Mr. Heitz, 37, most recently served in various roles at Vail Resorts, Inc... from October 2014 to November 2024.' Separately: 'Chief Accounting Officer Departure - Leslie Striedel, Chief Accounting Officer, will step down from her role, effective June 30, 2025.' CEO: David Barry was appointed CEO of Pursuit Hospitality and Attractions, Inc. in December 2024 (per Item 10), with an Offer Letter dated October 20, 2024 — the SAME DAY as the GES sale agreement was signed.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B insider_vs_calendar + CFO/CAO change timing. A simultaneous CEO appointment + CFO change + CAO departure clustered tightly around a transformational divestiture is the highest-discrimination governance pattern in the framework. Check: (a) is the CEO offer letter date contemporaneous with the deal-signing date (Oct 20, 2024)? (b) does the CFO Effective Date coincide with the 10-K filing (i.e., the OUTGOING CFO signs the 10-K, the incoming CFO inherits the going-forward forecast)? (c) does the CAO departure (June 30, 2025) leave the standalone company without its long-tenured accounting officer at the start of the first full reporting period under the new structure?
rfm_tuples.M_value: CONFIRMED: (a) Barry's offer letter is dated October 20, 2024, EXACTLY the GES purchase-agreement signing date — the new CEO was selected the same day the transformation was committed; (b) the 2024 10-K is signed March 17, 2025 by Ingersoll as outgoing CFO (her Effective Date = filing date) — the OUTGOING CFO certifies the FY24 numbers while the INCOMING CFO Heitz (37 yrs old, jumped from Vail Resorts VP-level role four weeks before the appointment) inherits the standalone-company forecast; (c) Striedel (CAO since 2014, 11-year tenure including the Crestview preferred deal in 2020) leaves June 30, 2025 — exactly the start of peak Q3 reporting period. NO Q4 2024 or Q1 2025 Rule 10b5-1 adoptions or terminations disclosed by any director/officer.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Three top finance/executive roles changing within six months of the GES sale and the rebrand creates a 'fresh team, no-historical-numbers-accountability' configuration. The pattern is classic: outgoing CFO signs the FY24 historicals (which she owns), incoming CFO sets the standalone-Pursuit guidance baseline (no incumbency burden), CAO (the deep institutional accountant) exits before the first full FY25 audit cycle. This is not fraudulent — Heitz is a credible Vail Resorts hire and Barry has run the Pursuit segment since 2015 — but the cluster + the absence of any pre-disclosure-window 10b5-1 plan adoption (which executives commonly file before transitions) is a Mode-B tell that the new team wants flexibility before committing to a trading plan.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As a result of our most recent long-lived assets and goodwill impairment analysis performed as of October 31, 2024, we determined that the carrying value of certain assets at our Las Vegas Flyover attraction asset group were not recoverable and were in excess of fair value and we recorded asset impairment charges of $27.5 million. Additionally, we recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $14.0 million associated with our Flyover attractions reporting unit.' 'The excess of the estimated fair value over the carrying value for our reporting units with reported goodwill... for the Banff Jasper Collection and the Alaska Collection was significant and Glacier Park Collection was 11%.' Plus $5.5M asset impairment on the cancelled Flyover Canada Toronto facility lease.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: forward-impairment probability + auditor critical-audit-matter cross-check. A 11% cushion is by definition fragile (typical disclosure threshold is 'less than 20%'); combined with already-impaired Flyover reporting unit, the question is whether the auditor flagged this. Cross-check Deloitte's Critical Audit Matter section to see WHICH reporting units the auditor specifically called out as requiring especially challenging judgments.
rfm_tuples.M_value: DELOITTE'S CRITICAL AUDIT MATTER explicitly names THREE areas: 'Flyover Attractions and Glacier Park Collection reporting units and Las Vegas Flyover Attraction asset group' — i.e., the EXACT three areas where management already took $46.5M of impairment in FY24 ($14M Flyover goodwill + $27.5M Flyover Las Vegas asset). The auditor signed off on the FY24 carrying values but flagged that 'performing audit procedures to evaluate the reasonableness of management's assumptions and estimates related to selection of the discount rates and forecasts required a high degree of auditor judgment and an increased extent of effort, including the need to involve our fair value specialists.' Total continuing-ops goodwill $103.3M ($60M Banff Jasper, $24M Flyover, $17M Glacier Park, $3M Alaska); $20.2M accumulated impairment vs $6.2M at YE23.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: An 11% goodwill cushion at Glacier Park Collection + a Critical Audit Matter that names Glacier Park as one of three reporting units requiring fair-value-specialist involvement = high probability of FY25 impairment if Glacier visitor traffic softens. Flyover Attractions has already taken $14M of goodwill impairment AND is also on the CAM — and the underlying Las Vegas Flyover has visible economic distress (full asset-group writedown in 2024). The fact that DELOITTE explicitly flagged THE SAME three reporting units where management impaired in 2024 is the auditor's way of telling readers 'we are not confident the rest of this goodwill is durable through one bad year.' Honestly disclosed (this is good) — but materially escalates downside risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On July 22, 2024, Jasper National Park was closed and evacuated due to wildfire activity, and a wildfire entered the Jasper townsite on July 24, 2024... Due to this road closure, the Maligne Lake Cruises did not reopen during the remainder of the 2024 season but will reopen for the 2025 season... We incurred total costs at our properties affected by the Jasper wildfires of approximately $21.5 million, all of which are deemed probable of recovery through our insurance. During 2024, we received approximately $13 million in insurance proceeds as a partial settlement... an additional amount of approximately $3.9 million received subsequent to December 31, 2024. As of December 31, 2024, the remaining balance in the insurance receivable of approximately $8.5 million represents costs that are deemed probable of recovery.' Hospitality 2024 occupancy fell from 70.3% (FY23) to 63.8% (FY24); Banff Jasper Collection revenue declined $9.0M YoY ($183.7M -> $174.7M, -4.9%).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: insurance-recovery and Maligne reopening verification. MODE B: business-interruption magnitude beyond the disclosed $21.5M physical loss; check Banff Jasper Collection revenue trajectory and ask what happens if Jasper visitor traffic in 2025 does NOT rebound to 2023 levels. Banff Jasper Collection is the company's largest segment ($174.7M of $366.5M = 47.7% of revenue) and the Maligne Lake Cruise alone is a Trip Advisor Travelers' Choice attraction that lost an entire summer.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K claims insurance recovery progressing ($13M received in 2024, $3.9M after YE, $8.5M still outstanding). Q1 2025 10-Q (filed May 9, 2025) UPDATES this: 'As of March 31, 2025, the remaining insurance receivable balance relating to the Jasper wildfires of approximately $2.2 million represents costs that are deemed probable of recovery, compared to $8.5 million as of December 31, 2024.' Plus $1.8M received subsequent to March 31, 2025. So insurance recovery is on track and credible. CRITICAL FORWARD SIGNAL from Q1 2025 10-Q: same-store attraction visitors DECLINED 6.1% YoY ('primarily attributable to the Sky Lagoon attraction, which had experienced exceptionally strong demand in the prior year'). Banff Jasper Collection Q1 2025 revenue $17.4M vs $18.1M Q1 2024 = (3.7%) DECLINE. This is BEFORE peak summer Jasper recovery test.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The insurance recovery story is honest and tracking — $21.5M of losses, $19M+ recovered by Q1 2025. The Mode-A check passes. But the Mode-B forward signal is concerning: Banff Jasper Q1 2025 is DOWN YoY pre-peak-season, and same-store attractions visitors are down 6.1% (Sky Lagoon comp normalization). With 77% of revenue in Q2/Q3 and the Maligne Lake Cruise / Columbia Icefield needing to recapture lost 2024 demand from Jasper townsite recovery, FY25 hinges on a Jasper rebound that is NOT visible in the pre-peak Q1 print. The 11% Glacier Park goodwill cushion and Flyover CAM further amplify the asymmetry.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We believe that our existing sources of liquidity will be sufficient to fund operations and projected capital outlays for at least the next 12 months and the longer term.' Total available liquidity as of Dec 31, 2024 = $49.7M (cash only — pre-2025 Revolver). Subsequent event: 'On January 3, 2025, we entered into a Credit Agreement (the 2025 Credit Agreement)... provides for a $200 million revolving credit facility (the 2025 Revolving Credit Facility), with a maturity of January 3, 2030.' Q1 2025 10-Q: cash $22.8M + $189.3M revolver capacity = $212.1M total liquidity.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: liquidity sufficiency claim. Standard 'at least the next 12 months and longer term' language; verify against debt maturities + capex + seasonal cash burn. MODE B: cash-burn trajectory and the fact that Q1 burns roughly half of YE cash; check whether revolver draws begin pre-peak-season.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total debt (continuing ops, excl finance leases) Dec 31 2024 = $14.7M (tiny — Jasper Term Loan $11.6M, Flyover Iceland $3.4M). Annual maturities $1M/yr through 2027, $11.6M in 2028. 2025 Revolving Credit Facility: $200M capacity, 5-yr maturity (Jan 3, 2030). Q1 2025 10-Q confirms only $5.0M drawn by March 31, 2025 + $5.7M LCs = $189.3M available. FY25 planned capex $70-75M (incl $38-43M growth projects). Q1 2025 operating cash flow was negative $24.4M (vs negative $22.4M Q1 2024). LIQUIDITY IS GENUINELY ABUNDANT given the small absolute debt and large undrawn revolver — Mode-A claim is well-supported. Cash burn of $26.9M in Q1 is seasonally normal (77% of revenue Q2/Q3); the revolver fills the seasonal gap.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Unlike the FUN/JACK pattern, PRSU's liquidity claim is honest and conservatively true. The GES sale proceeds were used to pay down the high-yield 2021 Credit Facility (a 10.5% interest rate Term Loan B!), leaving a near-debt-free entity with a 5-year $200M revolver. Even with $70-75M capex and seasonal cash burn, the company has 2-3+ years of runway without operating cash flow improvement. This is the cleanest balance sheet in the SP600-removal/control cohort and materially de-risks PRSU from a liquidity standpoint compared to pre-divestiture Viad.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On July 18, 2020, one of our off-road Ice Explorers was involved in an accident while enroute to the Athabasca Glacier, resulting in three fatalities and multiple other serious injuries. We immediately reported the accident to our relevant insurance carriers... In May 2023, we resolved charges from the Canadian office of Occupational Health and Safety in relation to this accident, resulting in fines and related payments in an aggregate amount of $0.5 million Canadian dollars (approximately $0.3 million U.S. dollars). We continue to manage our legal defense of various claims from the victims and their families. In addition, we believe that our reserves and, subject to customary deductibles, our insurance coverage is sufficient to cover potential claims related to this accident.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: legal-reserves disclosure adequacy. The 2020 Ice Explorer rollover (3 fatalities, multiple serious injuries) is a class-action-vulnerable mass-casualty event; OHS settled but civil claims remain pending five years later. MODE B: derive whether the $0.3M OHS settlement vs probable civil-liability magnitude is correctly reserved. Three wrongful-death + serious-injury claims in a Canadian provincial court with insurance carriers but customary-deductibles language is the kind of contingency where the 'sufficient reserves' assertion is verifiable only ex post.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K explicitly says civil claims from victims/families are STILL being defended as of March 17, 2025 — 56 months post-accident. The 'sufficient reserves and insurance coverage' claim is qualitative; no specific reserve amount or upper bound disclosed. Sector comparison: amusement/attractions wrongful death + serious-injury settlements typically range $5-15M per fatality + $1-3M per serious injury for the type of catastrophic event involved. Three fatalities plus 'multiple other serious injuries' could plausibly aggregate to $30-60M of exposure; deductibles language could leave some retention. Note 23 of the 10-K (referenced) would need full review for reserve specifics — not reachable in this extract.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The legacy 2020 Ice Explorer accident is honestly disclosed but the magnitude of contingent liability is opaque. Five years post-accident, civil claims remain unresolved. The 'sufficient reserves' assertion is unverifiable from public disclosure, and the underlying business RUNS THE SAME Columbia Icefield Adventure attraction with similar vehicles — a future accident-class risk that compounds. Not a deal-breaker, but a Mode B catch worth noting given the Banff Jasper Collection is the largest segment and the Ice Explorer/Columbia Icefield is one of its trophy attractions.

rfm_tuples.R: Auditor: 'We have served as the Company's auditor since at least 1929; however, an earlier year could not be reliably determined.' /s/ Deloitte & Touche LLP, Tempe, Arizona, March 17, 2025. No auditor disagreements disclosed (Item 9). 'Our independent registered public accounting firm, Deloitte & Touche LLP, has issued a report relating to our audit of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting' (Item 9A) — unqualified ICFR opinion.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: auditor_history + auditor_change_tracker. Verify tenure and rotation history; verify no Item 9 disagreements. MODE B: assess whether a 96+-year auditor tenure across a major restructuring + name change + management refresh constitutes constructive entrenchment that could lower professional skepticism.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deloitte tenure: 'since at least 1929' = 96+ years. Tempe, Arizona office (Pursuit corporate office is Denver/Scottsdale, AZ region). Unqualified opinions on both FY24 financial statements AND ICFR. NO Item 9 changes/disagreements. SOLE Critical Audit Matter = goodwill/long-lived asset impairment for Flyover Attractions + Glacier Park Collection + Las Vegas Flyover (the same three areas already impaired in 2024). PCAOB Form AP Auditor Firm ID 34.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Deloitte tenure of 96+ years is the longest auditor relationship in the universe — comparable to JACK's Deloitte tenure but even older. Combined with no disagreements, no rotation churn, and a CAM that the auditor used to flag forward impairment risk (rather than rubber-stamp), this is a CLEAN auditor signature. The Mode-B concern about entrenched-auditor low skepticism is partially offset by the fact that Deloitte EXPLICITLY called out the same reporting units management impaired — i.e., the auditor is signaling residual concern. Net PASS — but the 96-year tenure is the kind of relationship that should rotate.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the three months ended December 31, 2024, no director or officer of the Company adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement or non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.' Q1 2025 10-Q: 'During the quarter ended March 31, 2025, no director or officer of the Company adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement or non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.' Stock-based comp: PSUs granted in 2024 at $57.82 grant-date fair value (vs $34.62 prior-year balance) — i.e., the new PSU cohort is being granted at a 67% higher reference price than the unvested 2023 grants.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar. No 10b5-1 adoption around the GES sale, no termination around the price recovery, no Q1 2025 adoptions. PSU grant price step-up to $57.82 implies management VIEWS the post-divestiture stock price as the appropriate baseline for future performance hurdles — but the absence of 10b5-1 plans during a major transformation is itself the tell. Insiders are keeping discretionary trading flexibility through the rebrand window.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two consecutive disclosure windows with ZERO 10b5-1 adoptions/terminations (Q4 2024 and Q1 2025). PSU grant-date fair value 2024 = $57.82 (151,967 shares granted) vs 2023 balance avg $34.62 (i.e., 67% step-up in reference price). 2024 PSU vesting payouts = 73,919 shares at $32.89 avg grant price ($3.0M payout, paid in shares). Existing PSU balance Dec 31 2024 = 272,641 shares avg $46.23 fair value. CEO Barry, new CFO Heitz, outgoing CFO Ingersoll, departing CAO Striedel — none disclosed any 10b5-1 plan adoption during the transformation window.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Absence of any 10b5-1 plan adoption across two reporting windows that spanned (a) the announcement and close of a $535M divestiture, (b) preferred conversion at $42.50/share, (c) the rebrand, (d) the CEO/CFO/CAO transition, AND (e) the +18% YTD stock gain through Q1 2025 — is a deliberate choice to preserve discretionary insider trading flexibility during the highest-information-asymmetry window in years. Combined with PSU grants RESET at a higher base price ($57.82) right after the value-unlocking GES sale, the optics are that insiders have positioned themselves to (a) benefit from the upside reset, (b) avoid pre-committing to sales via 10b5-1 plans. Not fraudulent — but the Mode-B insider-vs-calendar signal is yellow.

rfm_tuples.R: Currency / international exposure: 'During 2024, our international operations accounted for approximately 67% of our consolidated revenue.' Foreign currency translation losses: cumulative $(62.9)M in stockholders' equity (vs $(35.3)M YE23; YoY swing of $(27.6)M). 'A hypothetical change of 10% in the Canadian dollar exchange rate would result in a change to 2024 income from continuing operations before income taxes of approximately $3.2 million.' 'A hypothetical change of 10% in the Icelandic Krona exchange rate would result in a change to 2024 income from continuing operations before income taxes of approximately $1.5 million.' Plus: 'Trade tensions or restrictions on free trade, including the recent escalation in tariffs following the recent U.S. presidential and congressional elections, could exacerbate these effects.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: FX hedging absence + tariff/trade-war exposure. The risk factor language about 'recent escalation in tariffs following the U.S. presidential and congressional elections' is a March 2025 disclosure of tariff policy concerns. Since 67% of revenue is international (mostly Canada + Iceland) AND the customer base is largely US travelers TO international destinations, the company is exposed BOTH to FX translation AND to inbound-tourist demand sensitivity if US-Canada relations deteriorate. The 10-K confirms 'We do not currently hedge our equity risk arising from the translation of foreign denominated assets and liabilities... we do not currently hedge our net earnings exposure.' No forward contracts outstanding.
rfm_tuples.M_value: International revenue 67% of consolidated revenue ($246M of $366M). Cumulative translation loss in AOCI accelerated $(27.6)M during 2024 (vs +$7.6M during 2023). CAD weakness already cost ~$25M of book equity in one year. 10% CAD/ISK move = $4.7M sensitivity to operating income (>10% of FY24 operating income). NO FX hedges or forward contracts at YE24 or YE23. Q1 2025 10-Q reports same: no forward contracts; $46.1M of nonfunctional-currency long-term liabilities still on books. Tariff risk-factor language was ADDED to the FY24 10-K (vs FY23 10-K, which did not mention 'tariff escalation following elections').
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 67% international revenue with zero FX hedging is an unusual structural choice — most peers with comparable exposure hedge at least 25-50% of forward operating income. Pursuit's choice to remain unhedged means the 2024 CAD weakness directly translated into $27.6M of equity erosion, and the new tariff/trade-war risk factor (specifically called out as a post-election concern) is unhedged. With Banff Jasper Collection (CAD-denominated) being 47.7% of revenue, even a 5% CAD weakening creates a $4.4M+ pre-tax income drag. Combined with the Q1 2025 attraction-visitor decline of 6.1%, this leaves PRSU exposed to a compound hit: CAD weakness + reduced US-Canada cross-border travel demand if tariff/border tensions intensify. Mode-B catch: management disclosed the tariff risk factor but offered no mitigation framework.

rfm_tuples.R: Claim evolution: 10-K (filed March 17, 2025) statements about 2025 outlook vs Q1 2025 10-Q (filed May 9, 2025, ~7 weeks after 10-K). 10-K Capital Expenditures: 'As of December 31, 2024, we have planned capital expenditures of approximately $70 million to $75 million for the next 12 months.' 10-K liquidity: 'sufficient to fund operations and projected capital outlays for at least the next 12 months and the longer term.' 10-K goodwill: '...Glacier Park Collection was 11%... If our adjusted expectations of the operating results of our reporting units do not materialize... additional goodwill impairment charges in the future, which may be material.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B claim_evolution: compare 10-K assertions to Q1 2025 10-Q updates, especially for capex, liquidity, goodwill testing, attendance trends, Jasper recovery progress, and the new tariff risk language.
rfm_tuples.M_value: RESULTS OF CLAIM EVOLUTION: (1) CapEx — 10-K said $70-75M FY25; 10-Q reaffirms same $70-75M (consistent). (2) Liquidity — 10-K said 'sufficient for 12 months and longer'; 10-Q shows $212.1M liquidity vs $49.7M at YE24, materially STRENGTHENED via $200M revolver activation. (3) Goodwill — 10-Q explicitly states 'We do not believe there have been any significant changes to the outlook for the future years or to the risk profile of our reporting units that would indicate that goodwill impairment testing should have been performed as of March 31, 2025' — this is the management ASSERTION that no interim test is needed despite the 11% Glacier Park cushion. (4) Attendance — 10-K reported FY24 same-store visitor change of +2.1%; 10-Q Q1 2025 same-store visitor change is NEGATIVE 6.1% — a 8.2-point reversal in the operating KPI management itself called the 'primary' driver. (5) Jasper recovery — insurance receivable down from $8.5M to $2.2M (good, on track). (6) Tariff language — 10-K added new risk factor about post-election tariffs; 10-Q risk factors section incorporates by reference (no new disclosure).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The most meaningful Mode-B claim_evolution finding: same-store attractions visitors went from +2.1% FY24 to -6.1% Q1 2025 — an 8.2-point swing in the KPI management calls 'primary.' Even with the Sky Lagoon comp normalization explanation, this is a HEADWIND going into the peak summer season, and the company chose NOT to interim-test goodwill for Glacier Park (11% cushion) despite the negative comp print. The decision to assert 'no significant changes' to the goodwill outlook in the Q1 10-Q — when the Q1 visitor data clearly is materially weaker than FY24 trajectory — is a Mode-B disclosure-evasion tell. Not fraudulent (FY25 Q2/Q3 will be the actual test), but the omission of any explicit pre-summer caution language is the kind of optimistic framing that recurs in stressed-cohort filings.

summary: PRSU presents an unusual profile: a structurally cleaner standalone entity (near-zero net debt, $200M undrawn 5-year revolver, GES sale gain $421.9M, no going-concern risk) wrapped inside a textbook 'fresh start' reset that is bundled with three high-discrimination Mode-B tells: (1) full C-suite transition timed to the transformation (CEO offer letter dated same day as GES deal signing; outgoing CFO Ingersoll signs FY24 historicals on her last day; new 37-year-old CFO Heitz from Vail Resorts inherits the standalone forecast; CAO Striedel exits before Q3 peak audit cycle) with ZERO Rule 10b5-1 plan adoptions across two disclosure windows; (2) the same-store attractions-visitor KPI swung from +2.1% FY24 to -6.1% Q1 2025 (8.2-point reversal in management's own self-identified 'primary' performance driver), yet Q1 10-Q asserts no goodwill-outlook change is needed despite Glacier Park Collection sitting at an 11% cushion (one of three reporting units Deloitte explicitly named in its CAM); (3) 67% international revenue is entirely unhedged into a freshly-added risk factor about post-election tariff escalation, while CAD weakness already cost $27.6M of equity in 2024. CLEAN/PASS signals offsetting the short thesis: liquidity is genuinely abundant; Deloitte 96-year auditor relationship has no disagreements; insurance recovery for Jasper wildfire is tracking ($19M+ of $21.5M received); no going-concern language; the GES sale is real economic deleveraging at a 10.5% Term Loan cost. Under the honesty-alpha framework: PRSU is not 'lying' — the disclosures are largely candid (Glacier Park 11% cushion stated; auditor CAM signaling forward concern; tariff risk factor added; Q1 visitor decline reported in 10-Q). What IS happening is selective optimistic framing of a transformation that has not yet been tested by a full peak season under the new structure, layered with a governance refresh that maximizes the new team's narrative discretion. Net composite: weak-moderate negative signal — meaningfully cleaner than JACK/CALY/FUN but with enough Mode-B yellow flags (executive cluster + 10b5-1 absence + attendance reversal + omitted interim impairment test) to warrant tagging rather than dismissal.
